title: Dynamic Commitment Recommender for Dedicated Pools (Commit Impact Explorer)
creator: Anika Shah
description:
Problem: Customers with Dedicated pools often over-provision commit levels to avoid throttles during rare peaks, increasing unit costs. Existing tooling reports utilization but does not offer a cost-aware, confidence-scored suggestion that ties a proposed commit delta to SLA risk and projected monthly savings.

Goal: Build a recommendation engine and Console view (Commit Impact Explorer) that: 1) analyzes historical per-pool utilization and request tail behavior, 2) simulates commit changes against SLOs (p99 latency, request-drop rate, throughput), 3) outputs a recommended commit delta with confidence and suggested hedging (safety buffer), and 4) surfaces expected monthly cost impact and rollback triggers.

Proposal overview:
- Offline analysis pipeline: aggregate 90/95/99th utilization by minute/hour, queue depths, failed-attach/overflow events, and model-variant mappings for each dedicated pool over a trailing 90d window.
- Simulation engine: run a fast-forward simulation that replays traffic with varied commit levels and autoscale policies (fixed, reactive, predictive) to estimate SLO risk and percent-of-requests penalized.
- Recommendation output: for each pool provide: recommended_commit_delta (GPUs or slots), confidence_score (A..E), projected_monthly_savings_usd, risk_profile (low/medium/high), suggested_hedge_ratio (e.g., +10% for weekday peaks), and rollback_triggers (e.g., p99 latency increase +15% for 24h).
- UI: Commit Impact Explorer in Console with interactive slider to preview commit changes, time-window selector, and a cost-savings forecast chart. Link each recommendation to the billing delta and to a one-click change API endpoint (/api/v1/dedicated/pools/:id/commit-recommendation/apply).
- Policy integration: recommendations respect contractual minimums, reserved commitment tiers, and region constraints. Suggestions are labeled "safe", "conservative", or "aggressive".

Metrics and success criteria:
- Correctness: simulated SLO breach rate <= 2% difference vs canary replays in sandbox environment.
- Business impact: ≥10% median monthly cost savings for top 30% of customers that adopt suggestions.
- Adoption: 20 customers apply automated recommendations within 3 months of launch.
- Telemetry: every recommendation includes traceable events (generated, previewed, applied, rolled back).

Data sources:
- Serving telemetry: per-request latency, token counts, KV cache hit/miss, attach/overflow events (ENG-40900 ingest pipeline).
- Billing: committed capacity invoices and usage-based line items (dependency on ENG-41421 ingestion of billing metrics).
- Pool metadata: model mapping, hardware type, autoscale policy, reserved tier.

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Data aggregation: SQL/Presto queries + daily rollups; baseline dashboards for utilization percentiles (owner: Data Team, blocker: ENG-40900).
2) Simulation prototype: Python service that replays sample traces and produces recommendation outputs (owner: Miguel).
3) API & policy layer: new endpoints to fetch and apply recommendations; validations for contractual limits (owner: infra).
4) Console: Commit Impact Explorer with preview slider, cost chart, and justification text (owner: front-end).
5) Canary and measurement: internal sandbox customers for 2-week canary to validate simulation -> real-world delta.

Acceptance criteria:
- End-to-end flow from data ingestion to UI preview works for at least 3 dedicated pools.
- Recommendation schema documented and stable (versioned).
- Simulation accuracy validated against replayed traces (difference within target).
- Console offers preview + one-click apply that creates a change request and records telemetry.

Risks & mitigations:
- Inaccurate billing mapping could show misleading savings: require billing ingestion dependency before any cost projection.
- Sudden workload pattern shifts could make suggestions unsafe: include conservative hedging and a rapid rollback policy + automated fallback to original commit.
- Customer trust: provide clear conservatism labeling and a dry-run mode that only simulates cost changes until customer opts in.

Open questions:
- What is the canonical definition of "safety buffer" across different hardware types? (ask Platform ML).
- Should recommendations be exposed via webhook to account owners? (Product to decide).

Deliverables:
- Recommendation engine service (v1), simulation test harness, API endpoints, Console Commit Impact Explorer, telemetry dashboard for recommendations, documentation for customers and sales playbook.
